en: The Buddha Spoke the *Tudu Sūtra*.
Translator’s name lost; now appended to the Eastern Jin Records.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī. In that kingdom, there was a brahmin.
His name was Doudiao, and he had a son named Gu.
Doudiao was a man of urgent and wicked character who constantly delighted in reviling others; after his death, he returned to become a dog for his own family, named Lue.

As for his son Gokula, he was so fond of this dog that he bound it with golden chains; he always provided it with woolen rugs and fine carpets when it lay on its bed, and fed it exquisite food from golden plates.
When Gu came out to the market, the Buddha passed by his gate, and a white dog barked at him.
The Buddha immediately said:
"In your ordinary state, you raise your paws and bark; now you have turned into a dog and are barking at me. You do not know shame."
The dog then fled in shame; holding its head and face beneath the bed, it wept with tears flowing.
After the Buddha had departed, the dog no longer ascended the bed upon which he had lain, but instead slept on the ground, refusing to eat the food offered to it.
Tāṇḍya came from outside; seeing that the dog did not eat, he asked the household, "Why is the dog like this?
The household replied:
"Just now a certain śramaṇa passed by; I do not know what he said.
Because of this, the dog ran under the bed and lay on the ground, refusing to eat its food.
Gu replied:
"Where is the śramaṇa going?
The man replied,
"He is going east."
Gou immediately followed in pursuit and caught up with him.
While the Buddha was preaching the sutra to the bhikṣus beneath a tree, he saw Gou approaching from afar and addressed the bhikṣus:
"Gou is coming; he has not reached the Path, and upon death he shall fall into hell."
The bhikṣus asked the Buddha,
"For what reason does one fall into hell?
The Buddha said:
"This man came with evil intent, wishing to harm others; he shall surely fall into hell.
When Gu reached the Buddha's presence, he asked:
"Which śramaṇa passed by my gate just now and cursed my dog?"
"Make him not eat and not lie down in that place.
The Buddha then replied,
"When I passed by your door, a white dog barked at me, and I immediately said:"
"You usually raise your paws and roar, yet now you have turned around to intimidate me like a dog! Do you have no shame!
At this, the dog fled in shame, bowing its head beneath the bed and weeping with tears streaming forth.
Gavāṃpati asked the Buddha,
"What is this dog to me?
The Buddha said:
"There is no need to ask; hearing it would cause you displeasure.
Gu replied, "I will listen; please speak for me."
The Buddha said,
"It was the speaker who caused you to become angry. Gu replied:
“I do not dare to feel anger.
I wish to hear it.
The Buddha said:
"This is your father, Doudiao.
Gu said, "When my father Doudiao was in the world, he was learned in the Confucian and Daoist classics; he did not become a dog."
The Buddha said:
"It was solely because you were arrogant regarding what you knew that you were reborn as a dog.
Do you wish to know for certain whether this is indeed your father?"
Returning home, he spoke to the dog, saying:
"If you are truly my father, Doudiao, you should eat from your former vessel.
If you are truly my father, you should lie down in your former place."
"If you are truly my father, you should show me the location where the precious treasures and goods you formerly possessed are hidden.
The valley-dweller then returned home and called to the dog,
saying, "Mule!"
"If you are indeed my father, Daudiao, you shall eat this food.
The dog immediately ate the food.
Guo spoke again:
“Mule! If you are truly my father, you should lie down in your former place.
The dog immediately lay down in its former place.
Gu replied, "Mule! If you are truly my father,
you should show me the location of the precious treasures and goods you possessed in the past."
The dog then used its mouth to point beneath the right leg of the bed and scratched the ground with its two front paws to indicate it.
Gu then dug up the spot where the mule had scratched and obtained a vast quantity of rare treasures and precious objects.
Gou was greatly filled with joy and returned to where the Buddha was.
Seeing him from afar, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"Now Gou is coming; though he did not reach the Way, he who died has been reborn in the heavens."
The bhikṣus asked the Buddha,
“By what causes and conditions is one reborn in the heavens?
The Buddha said:
"Because this person has come with a benevolent mind, they shall be reborn in the heavens.
When Gou arrived at the Buddha's dwelling, he went before the Buddha, prostrated himself in worship, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is indeed as the Buddha has said."
Gu replied again to the Buddha, saying:
“When people dwell in the world, for what reason are there some who have long lives and others who do not?
For what reason are there some who have many ailments and others who have few?”
Why is it that some faces alone possess a beautiful complexion while others have an ugly complexion?
Why is it that some alone are noble while others are lowly?
Why is it that some alone are charming while others are uncharming?
"Why is it that there are only some who are wealthy and some who are poor?
Why is it that there are only some who are wise and some who are foolish?
The Buddha told Gu:
"If a person in this world delights in killing and lacks a heart of compassion, upon death they will enter hell;
when their retribution in hell is exhausted, they will be reborn as a human, yet they will have a short lifespan."
If a person in this world refrains from killing and possesses a heart of compassion, they will ascend to heaven upon death;
when descending from heaven to be born among humans, they will enjoy long life.
If a person in this world delights in strife and disorder, wielding knives and staves to intimidate others, they will enter hell after death.
When their retribution for sins in hell has ended and they are reborn as humans, they will be frequently ill.
Humans in the world delight in harmony and do not threaten others with weapons or staves; such people, upon death, are born in the heavens.
When they descend from heaven to be born among humans, they will have little illness.

In this world, people delight in anger and resentment; they become angry upon hearing pleasant words and angry upon hearing unpleasant words. They become angry seeing the virtuous and angry seeing the foolish. Failing to distinguish between good and evil, they seek only to be wrathful, and after death they enter the hells.
When their retribution for those crimes in hell is exhausted, they are reborn as humans, yet their faces are colorless, withered, and sallow.
If a person in this world is free from hatred and anger, honoring the wise when they see them and practicing patience toward the foolish, they will ascend to heaven upon death.
When descending from heaven to be born again among humans, their facial complexion will always be fine, they will be harmonious with others, and their mind will be virtuous and good.

Those people in the world who are not compliant—those who do not rise when seeing an elder, who are unfilial toward their parents, and who lack respect and affection for their parents—will always harbor resentment toward those who are filial, respectful toward their parents and elders, and upon death will enter hell.
When their retribution in hell is exhausted and they are reborn as humans, they will again be non-compliant and loathed by all people.

In this world, people are filial toward their parents and respectful toward their elders. If there are those who are unfilial or disrespectful toward their elders, one should go and instruct them. One who delights in speaking virtuous words to others for their benefit will ascend to heaven upon death;
descending from heaven to be born again in the human realm, they will be loved and respected by others.
If a person in this world is arrogant and disrespectful toward elders, acting willfully and obstinately, they will enter hell after death;
when their punishment in hell is completed, they will again become human, but as one of low station.
If a person in this world is not arrogant and always respects those who are venerable, and does not act with overbearing insolence toward others, they will ascend to heaven upon death;
descending from heaven to be born again among humans, they will consequently become a venerable person.

In this world, people are stingy and greedy; though wealthy, they do not bestow gifts upon the poor, they do not care for their kinsmen, and they take no pleasure in giving. They covet food and drink, yet they do not give to śramaṇas or practitioners of the Way, nor even dare to satisfy themselves.
Upon death, they enter hell; when their retribution in hell is exhausted, they are reborn as humans, but immediately become poor, lowly, and beggars.

If a person in this world is free from the mind of stinginess and greed, whether rich or poor, they delight in giving to śramaṇas and practitioners of the Way, bestowing gifts upon the needy and cherishing their kinsmen; if they always eat their fill themselves, they will ascend to heaven after death.
When descending from heaven to be reborn in the world, they will possess wealth and joy, and be respected and loved by others.

If a person in this world hears of those who have mastered the scriptures and attained lofty heights—whether they be śramaṇas or Daoist practitioners—and yet does not take pleasure in going to them to inquire about the Way that transcends the world, harboring instead a mind of envy toward their loftiness, such a person will enter hell after death;
when their punishment in hell has ended and they are reborn as a human, they will be immediately foolish and ignorant, no different from the ranks of animals.

If a person in this world hears of one who is renowned for their mastery of the scriptures and profound insight—such as a śramaṇa or a Daoist—and goes to them with a sincere desire to inquire about the matters of transcending the world, without harboring jealousy or craving such loftiness, they will ascend to heaven upon death.
Descending from heaven to be born among humans, they will be one who masters the scriptures and understands the Way, and will be honored and employed by all people.
The Buddha said: "Those who perform good deeds attain rebirth in heaven; those who commit evil fall into hell. If a person seeks long life, they obtain long life;

if they seek a short life, they obtain a short life. If they seek illness, they obtain illness; if they seek health, they obtain health. If they seek a beautiful countenance, they obtain a beautiful countenance; if they seek an ugly countenance, they obtain an ugly countenance. If they seek high status, they obtain high status; if they seek lowliness, they obtain lowliness. If they seek charm, they obtain charm; if they seek lack of charm, they obtain lack of charm. If they seek wealth, they obtain wealth; if they seek poverty, they obtain poverty. If they seek wisdom, they obtain wisdom; if they seek folly, they obtain folly."

When people perform good or evil deeds in this world, it is like planting grain and obtaining grain, planting wheat and obtaining wheat, or planting rice and obtaining rice; by performing good one obtains good, and by performing evil one obtains evil.
Gou then withdrew and knelt down, saying:
"When I first came here, I saw that the dog would not eat, and I harbored anger toward it; this was due only to my ignorance.

What the Buddha has now spoken is like a blind man regaining his sight, a deaf man regaining his hearing, a person fallen into deep water being rescued, a madman recovering from his delusion, or a traveler in the darkness seeing the sun and moon."

"I pray that you will show me compassion before the Buddha and allow me to repent my transgressions. May you grant me your great grace, so that I may immediately undertake the five precepts and become an upāsaka.
The Buddha said:

"In future generations, there will be people who recite this sutra or hear its sound, whose hearts are moved with pity, whose hair stands on end, and whose tears immediately flow. Such persons shall all become disciples of Maitreya Buddha and attain deliverance from the world."
The Sūtra on Dautiya Spoken by the Buddha
